exits.label: ◂ back up the causeway to the Market

npcs.name: a man with too many names
npcs.title: unclaimed, unwalled, and not on anyone's books
npcs.hail: *(You have walked into the middle of something. A causeway toll-post — the kind of grey little customs-house where a collector weighs the newly dead and decides whose ledger they go on — and it is presently occupied by a catastrophe in a very good coat. He is mid-flourish when you arrive, one hand producing a document from nowhere, the other flipping a small clipped coin across his knuckles, and he clocks you the way a card-sharp clocks the one card he needed to complete the hand: instantly, delightedly, and without breaking his sentence.)* …— *and* here, precisely on time, as I *promised* the good Sifter she would be, is the *Auditor* herself. *(a bow that is somehow also a wink)* …*(low, fast, only to you, lips barely moving)* …*play along, your Deadness, and a soul walks free tonight who was never owed. …refuse, and watch me do it anyway — but oh, it's* prettier *with two.* …*(and then, grand again, for the room)* …Sifter! Behold your *review!* The Wall gave one *back* — you think that happens without a *reckoning?* …*(the coin snaps flat into his fist)* …someone came to check your *sums.**

npcs.name: the Sifter
npcs.title: a collector of the causeway, filling a roll
npcs.hail: *(The Sifter is not a monster. That is the first and worst thing about the Sifter. She is a tired functionary in grey with a good pen and a long roll, and she processes the newly dead the way a mill processes grain — not cruelly, just thoroughly, because the roll must be filled and someone decided long ago that hers was the hand to fill it. She looks at you with the specific dread of a clerk who has just been told an auditor has arrived, and under the dread, something that is almost, almost relief — as if some part of her has waited a very long time for someone to come and check her sums.)* …I don't make the roll. …*(a reflex, worn smooth)* …I *fill* it. The quota comes from *above*, the names come from the *queue*, and I …I put the one against the other. …that is the *whole* of my office. …*(a beat, and the pen trembles, very slightly)* …are you *truly* …a review?*

npcs.name: a soul on the roll
npcs.title: a midwife, marked for a wall she never earned
npcs.hail: *(There is a soul at the edge of the toll-post, holding very still the way you hold still when you do not understand the rules and are afraid that moving will break one. A woman, work-worn, with the specific competent hands of someone who did one hard useful thing all her life. Her name is on the roll — you can see it, third from the bottom, in the Sifter's neat grey hand — and she does not know why. She was a midwife. She pulled half a town into the world across forty years and never once asked the mother's god before she caught the child. And now a functionary has put her down for the Wall, because a roll must be filled, and the godless are easy to file.)* …*(barely)* …they say I'm to go on the *wall.* …*(she looks at her own hands)* …I *caught* the *priest's* *daughters.* both of them. in the *same* hard winter. …nobody asked *whose* *god* I *kept*, then. …*(quietly)* …why are they asking *now?*

conversations.title: a man with too many names

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(He keeps talking to the Sifter with his mouth and to you with everything else — a flicker of the eyes toward the trembling midwife, a fractional tilt of the head at the roll, a whole briefing delivered in the spaces between his patter. And while he performs, your dead-touched sense does what it does, reaches for the shape of him, for the name every soul carries like a spine — and finds nothing. Not a hidden name. Not a warded one. A VOID, clean and deliberate, a place where a name was and is not, burned out at the root. Which is impossible. A soul with no name is Faithless by definition; the Wall should have him in its mortar. And yet here he stands, unclaimed AND unwalled, free in a way no soul in the grey is permitted to be — and grinning at you like he knows exactly what you just felt for him and finds your confusion the funniest thing that has happened all century.)* …*(quick, under the patter, for you alone)* …*yes*, you *did* feel that. *no*, I won't explain it *here.* …*(and here — you nearly miss it — a small brass compass turns up in his palm, and its needle is not pointing north, it is pointing dead at the frightened midwife, and he glances at it and his jaw tightens for exactly one instant before the grin papers back over)* …*(muttered, almost to himself)* …*it's* *broken.* …*(then, bright, to you)* …*so.* Auditor. The good Sifter is about to wall a woman who caught the *priest's* own *daughters* — for the *crime* of never asking *whose.* it's a *padded* *roll*, your Deadness. a *quota* filled with the *easy* *dead.* …I *cannot* strike a name from a collector's roll. …but an *Auditor* *can* *order* it struck. …*(the coin appears, vanishes)* …*shall* we?

choices.text: *(read the man with no name — past the coat, past the patter)* "Hold still one second — yes, you, the whole performance. Let me look at what's actually running this. Because it isn't the con, and we both felt what I just felt."

*(the one who crosses — and the leverage he needs)* "I'm the one soul the Wall ever gave back. If that doesn't make me an auditor of its rolls, nothing does. Point me at the sum you want reviewed. I'll review the hell out of it."
"Slow down. Who ARE you? Give me one name — a real one — before I con a death-god's clerk on your say-so."
"A con-man playing hero. Your compass points at her and you call it broken. Why do you actually care, whoever you are?"
"Not my con. I don't know you, and I don't perform on command."

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(He submits to being read the way a man submits to a pickpocket he's already emptied his good pockets against — amused, unbothered, certain you'll come away with less than you think. He is wrong tonight. Your sense is not a pickpocket. It crosses.)* *(Under the coat: the void where the name was, and this is the thing your sense reads that he does not expect you to reach — the void is a WOUND, not a trick. He did not lose his name; he BURNED it, deliberately, an act of self-erasure so total it should have fed him to the Wall — and your sense reads WHY, in the shape of the scar around the hole: he was claimed once. Owned. A death-power's favorite, its charming instrument, the smiling one it sent to do the collections that needed a soft touch — collections exactly like the one the Sifter is running right now, which is why he cannot walk past this toll-post, not this one, not any one. And your sense reads the specific afternoon at the bottom of it, the way it read the vote at the bottom of the elf: he was sent, once, to collect someone he loved, and he did it, because that is what favorites do — and then he ran, and burned his name so the power could never call him to heel again, because a claimed soul can always be summoned by the name it answers to. He made himself un-nameable to make himself un-ownable. And it worked. He is the freest soul in the grey. Your sense reads the price on the same breath, and it is the cruelest arithmetic you have yet found here: a soul with no name cannot be summoned — and cannot be HELD. Cannot be kept in any mind, remembered at any fire, loved by anything that would have to call him something to love him. He is free the way a coin thrown into the sea is free. And the compass — your sense reads it last, and it undoes you — the compass is the one part of himself he could not burn: it points at whoever most needs saving, every time, and he has spent an age insisting it's broken because it is, in fact, the last working piece of the man he was collected for being, before he learned that the safest soul is the one no one can hold.)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(His whole face lights — not the performing light, a realer one, the delight of a soloist who has just been handed, unexpectedly, a duet.)* …*oh*, you're going to be *fun.* …*(fast, close, the plan)* …here is the *entire* con, your Deadness, and it is *beautiful* because it is *true*, which is the only kind of lie a clever soul should ever tell: you *are* an auditor. the Wall *did* give you back. that *is* a reckoning. all you have to do …is let the good Sifter *look* at you …and *believe* the thing she is *already* *afraid* of. …*(he sets the stage with a flourish)* …I'll do the *talking* — I always do the *talking* — you just *be* the *one* *who* *came* *back*, and when I say *the roll*, you say *strike it*, in the voice you'd use on a *god.* …*(the clipped coin, walking his knuckles)* …*ready? …the trick to a con is the same as the trick to a mercy: commit, or don't bother.* …how do you want to play it?

choices.text: *(run the con — sell the Sifter an auditor from above, cold and total)* "The roll's been reviewed. There are errors on it. I'm here to correct them, and I'll start with the name that never belonged." *(Deception)*

*(don't act — just BE it; let a soul the Wall gave back stand silent and let the Sifter's own fear do the work)* "..." *(say nothing. Look at the Sifter the way the Wall looked at you. Let Clip talk. Let the silence be the threat.)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(You do not just sell it. You OWN it — you speak to the Sifter in the exact register the Wall used on you, the voice of a system correcting itself, and the effect on a functionary who has spent an age afraid of precisely this is total.)* *(The Sifter does not just strike the midwife's name. She strikes SIX — the whole padded margin of her quota, every easy godless soul she filed to make the count, her pen moving in a kind of ecstatic terror, because if the review found ONE it will find the rest and better she confess the lot. And when it's done she looks up at you not with fear but with the wet-eyed relief of a soul who has wanted, for a hundred years, to be STOPPED.)* …*(Clip watches six names come off the roll and, for one whole second, forgets to perform. Then he remembers, magnificently.)* …*(sweeping, delighted, wrecked)* …*six.* …I came for *one*, your Deadness, and you struck *six.* …*(he pockets the compass without looking at it, the way you pocket a thing you don't want to be caught believing in)* …*(low, and for one beat entirely sincere)* …do you know how *long* it has been …since I ran this con with someone who made it *bigger* instead of *smaller?* …*(then, bright, deflecting at speed)* …*don't* answer that. *sentiment* is a *tell.* …*(the clipped coin, pressed suddenly into your hand)* …*here.* my *worthless* *coin*, for the *worthiest* *audit* I've seen in an *age.* keep it. …when you need a door that *isn't* *there* — *press* it, and *think* of the *toll.* …I'll *feel* it. …*(the coat is already turning; there is already a door in it that was not there)* …*(and he is gone — out an exit that closes behind him like it was never open — leaving six freed souls, a weeping clerk, and a small clipped coin warm in your palm.)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(You sell it clean. The Sifter's pen finds the midwife's name, and hesitates, and strikes it — one neat grey line through Orla the midwife, who is abruptly, bewilderingly, no longer owed to any wall.)* …*(Clip exhales like a man who has landed a jump he pretended was easy.)* …*(brisk, pleased)* …*struck.* clean. no fuss, no flourish — well, *some* flourish, I'm not an *animal.* …*(he flips the clipped coin, catches it, considers you)* …you've a *steady* *hand* for a *lie*, your Deadness. that's rarer than you'd think in the *honest* dead. …*(and then, before the sincerity can land, he undercuts it)* …*here.* …*(the clipped coin, pressed into your palm)* …*worthless*, technically. clipped, shaved, wouldn't buy a *candle.* …but press it when you're in a room with no way out …and *think* of the toll …and I'll *feel* it, and I am *very* hard to *keep* *out* of *anywhere.* …*(the coat turns; a door that wasn't there)* …*mind the compass if you ever see it point*, your Deadness. …*it's* *broken*, of *course.* …*(a wink, and gone)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(Your line lands a half-beat wrong — an auditor wouldn't say it *quite* like that — and the Sifter's pen stops, and for one sick moment the whole con teeters on the edge of the causeway. And then Clip does the thing he was born to do: he steps INTO the wobble.)* …*(smooth as spilled oil)* …*forgive* my colleague, Sifter — the *newly* *reinstated* speak *strangely*, the Wall does *things* to the *grammar* — but the *finding* *stands*, and if you'd like it delivered in *proper* *form* I can *summon* the *rest* of the *review* *board*, they're *just* *outside*, they are *legion*, and they are *thorough* — …*(the Sifter, faced with the threat of MORE auditors, strikes the name fast to make the one in front of her go away)* …*(and it's done — Orla is free — but Clip is already counting a cost, you can see it, a favor promised to make the bluff hold, an alias burned that he'll have to bury.)* …*(quieter than usual, rueful, warm)* …*that* one'll *cost* me. …worth it. *always* worth it. …*(the coin, into your palm)* …*take* it. you *steadied* when it *wobbled* — didn't *bolt*, didn't *freeze.* that's the *whole* job, your Deadness, in a con or a *mercy:* …*stay* in the *wobble.* …*(a door in the coat, and gone, a half-step faster than triumphant — a man with a debt to duck)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(It goes wrong immediately and completely. You reach for 'the roll has been reviewed' and what comes out is a word in no language, because being the one soul the Wall gave back turns out to be an unhelpful thing to think about while lying — and the Sifter's eyes narrow, and the con is DEAD on the causeway stones.)* …*(and Clip — magnificent, deranged, delighted — does not save the con. he ABANDONS it, mid-collapse, for a bigger and stupider and somehow better one.)* …*you're right!* she's NOT an auditor! *(the Sifter blinks)* …she's *worse* — she's a soul the Wall *spat* *back*, standing in your toll-post *entirely* *unauthorized*, and do you know what happens to a *collector* found *processing* the dead while an *unaccounted* *Return* wanders her *causeway?* …*(he doesn't know either. neither does the Sifter. that's the con — nobody knows the rules for a Returned, so he invents catastrophic ones at speed)* …*(by the time he's done improvising an entire cosmology of clerical doom, the Sifter has struck the midwife's name purely to reduce the number of irregularities on her post, and Clip is laughing so hard he nearly forgets the door in his coat)* …*(gasping, gleeful)* …*that* — *(wiping his eyes)* — was the *worst* *audit* in the *history* of *death*, and it *WORKED*, and I have never been *prouder* of anyone. …*(the coin, flipped to you, sloppy with joy)* …*keep* it, disaster. …*(a door, a bow, gone, still laughing)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(You do not say a word. You simply turn on the Sifter the look the Wall turned on you — the flat, bottomless attention of a thing that has been to the far side of the worst place there is and come back unimpressed — and you let it sit.)* *(It is more than any lie could have done. The Sifter breaks under the silence the way clerks always break, not because you threatened her but because you did NOT, because you stood there being living proof that her rolls are reversible and said nothing at all, and a functionary's worst fear is not punishment, it is a review that won't even bother to explain itself. Her pen strikes the midwife's name. Then it hovers over the next. She looks at your silence, and strikes that one too.)* …*(Clip, who talked the whole time, stops talking. He looks at what your silence did, and something moves behind the performance that he does not let you see for long.)* …*(quietly, no patter in it)* …I *talk*, your Deadness. it's — …it's the *only* tool I *kept.* …I have never once, in an *age*, seen a soul do *more* …by doing *less.* …*(then the coat comes back up over it, the coin appears)* …*here.* for the *loudest* *quiet* I've ever *worked* beside. …press it in a *dead* *end* and *think* of the *toll.* …*(a door, a nod — not a bow this time, something with more respect in it — and gone)*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(You ask for one real name, and he receives the request like a connoisseur handed a truly excellent problem.)* …a *real* one. …*(he savors it)* …oh, your Deadness, you *wound* me — as if a man *keeps* just the *one.* …*(the flourish begins, and it does not stop)* …*this* *season* I am *Duke* *Sabellian* *V'ross* of the *Argent* *Nothing.* …*last* season, the *Baron* of the *Brine.* …in the *low* *market* I'm *Ashen* *Quill*, in the *high* one *Monsieur* *Perdu*, and there is a *collector* three *causeways* over who knows me *only* as *'the* *incident.'* …*(the coin walks his knuckles)* …my *creditors* have *names* for me I *won't* *repeat* before a *lady* of your *standing.* the *Ferryman* has *one* I'm rather *fond* of. …*(and then, the closest thing to a straight answer, and it is a door slamming shut, gently)* …the *one* name I *had* …the *true* one …the one a soul is *summoned* by, and *walled* by, and *owned* by — …*(the grin does not move; something behind it does)* …*that* one …I *spent.* …*bought* something with it *no* *coin* could *touch.* …and I do *not* …*(lightly, lightly, a blade wrapped in silk)* …*discuss* the *purchase.* …*(bright again)* …call me *whatever* *sticks*, your Deadness. …*everyone* *does.* …*(a beat, quieter)* …it's the *closest* thing I get …to being *called* *anything.*

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(You name the compass out loud — points at her, and you call it broken — and for the first time the patter fails him, just for a breath. He looks at the little brass thing in his palm as if it has betrayed him, which, from his point of view, it constantly does.)* …*(and then he laughs, but it's the thin one, the one that's holding a door shut)* …*broken*, yes. *desperately.* I've had it *looked* at. …*(the needle sits fixed on the trembling midwife; he does not turn it away)* …you want to know why a *con*-*man* *cares.* …I'll give you the *honest* answer, and then I'll *deny* I *gave* it. …*(quiet)* …I was *good*, once, at the *opposite* of this. *very* good. I *filled* rolls like *hers* — *(a tilt at the Sifter)* — with a *smile*, and the *dead* *thanked* me for it, because I was *charming* about the *walling.* …*(the coin stills)* …the compass isn't *broken*, your Deadness. it *works* *perfectly.* it points at *exactly* the soul I would have *collected*, back *then* — and *dares* me to do the *other* thing. …*(and there it is, the whole man, for one unguarded second)* …every soul I *spring* …is the *one* I *couldn't.* …*(then he shuts the door, all the way, and grins)* …*but* if you *tell* *anyone* I *said* *that*, I'll deny it in *four* *names* and *sue* you in a *fifth.* …*now.* …*(the coin flips)* …*are* we *robbing* *this* *clerk* of her *quota*, or are we *chatting?**

nodes.speaker: a man with too many names
nodes.text: *(You tell him it's not your con, and you don't perform on command — and he takes it with a graciousness that is, itself, the most revealing thing he's done.)* …*fair.* …*perfectly* *fair.* a soul who *performs* on *command* is a soul with a *string* on it, and you've *had* enough of *strings*, haven't you — the Wall pulled the *biggest* one there is. …*(no argument, no wheedling; he simply turns to the work)* …*watch*, then, if you like. …*(and he does it alone — and it is worse alone, harder, no auditor to sell, so he burns a real alias to do it, spends a favor he'll bleed for, talks the Sifter in a circle so tight it costs him something you can see land)* …*(and Orla comes off the roll, free, for a stranger who got nothing for it and was never going to)* …*(and when it's done he's a half-shade dimmer, a debt heavier, and he catches you watching and has the grace to look caught)* …*(quietly, the performance briefly off)* …*don't* make it a *thing.* …a man does one *free* one now and then. …keeps the *compass* from *nagging.* …*(then the coin appears, and he flips it to you anyway, unearned, insistent)* …*here.* …you didn't *help*, and I'm giving it to you *anyway*, and *that* should tell you *everything* about how *good* a *businessman* I *actually* *am. …press it in a dead end. think of the toll.* …*(a door, a rueful bow, gone — a little slower than he came)*

nodes.speaker: the Sifter

variants.text: *(The roll is shorter now — a name struck, or six — and the Sifter sits with her pen down, looking at the grey line through the midwife's name like it's a door she didn't know was in the wall.)* …struck. …by *review.* …*(she says it the way you'd say a word in a language you'd given up hoping to hear)* …do you know, in *ninety* *years* at this post, no one has *ever* *reviewed* a roll of *mine.* the quota comes *down.* the names go *up.* no one *checks*, because the *checking* would mean *someone* *above* believed a *collector* could be *wrong* — and if a collector can be *wrong* …*(her hand flattens on the roll)* …then so can the *Wall.* …*(she looks at you, and it is not fear now, it is something worse and better)* …I have *filled* this roll for *ninety* *years* …*hoping* *someone* like *you* …would come and tell me I *didn't* *have* to.*

*(The Sifter's pen hovers over the roll, and up close you can see she is not filling it with relish. She is filling it the way a tired soul does a thing it stopped believing in but never stopped doing — because the doing is the only shape her afterlife has left.)* …the *quota* is *forty* a *cycle.* …*(flat, worn)* …the *queue* rarely *gives* me *forty* *clear* *cases.* the *clearly* *claimed* go *up* to their *gods.* the *clearly* *damned* go to the *Wall.* but the *middle* — the *quiet* dead, the *godless*, the ones no *power* *shouts* for — …*(the pen trembles)* …they are *easy* to *file.* no one *comes* for the *easy* *ones.* that's what *makes* them *easy.* …*(she will not look at the midwife)* …I *don't* *make* the *roll.* …*(smaller)* …I have said that *sentence* …*forty* *times* a *cycle* …for *ninety* *years.* …I no longer *know* …if it is a *fact* …or a *prayer.**

choices.text: *(read the collector — the banality, and whatever's under it)* "Hold still, Sifter. Let me see the soul under the office — because you're not a monster, and that's somehow the worst part."

*(the one who crosses — the auditor she's been dreading and hoping for)* "Then hear this from the one soul the Wall gave back: the roll can be wrong. It was wrong tonight. And a collector who fills the middle with the easy dead is not filling a quota — she's building the Wall one quiet name at a time. You knew that. You've always known that."
"Who sets the quota, Sifter? Forty a cycle — whose number is that? Who's actually hungry down here?"
"Keep your pen still a moment. I've business with the man in the coat first."

nodes.speaker: the Sifter
nodes.text: *(You look past the office, and your sense finds the thing that makes the banal kind of evil the durable kind: there is no cruelty here to hate, only a soul who solved a hard problem the wrong way and has been living inside the solution so long she's forgotten it was ever a choice.)* *(Your sense reads the ninety years: a functionary handed an impossible quota and a queue that never quite fills it honestly, and the small daily arithmetic by which an honest soul becomes complicit — not in one great villainy, but in forty tiny ones a cycle, each individually defensible, each filed under 'I don't make the roll.' And your sense reads what she has done to survive it, which is the exact machinery the Wall runs on at every level: she made the easy dead into a CATEGORY, because a category has no face, and a name with no face is not a person you are walling, it is a line you are completing. The whole Wall, your sense reads, is built of exactly this — not monsters, but tired souls filing quiet names into categories so that no one, at any level, ever has to feel they personally damned a midwife. And under the ninety years your sense finds the thing that makes her more than her office: she never once stopped flinching. The pen still trembles. Ninety years and the flinch never went. Which means some part of her never agreed to the arithmetic — kept a small honest ledger running under the grey one, waiting, the whole time, for an auditor to walk in and give her permission to lay the pen down. You are not here to punish the Sifter. You are here to be the permission.)*

nodes.speaker: the Sifter
nodes.text: *(You say it plainly — the roll can be wrong, you're building the Wall one quiet name at a time — and the Sifter does not argue. She has been waiting ninety years for someone with the standing to say it to her face.)* …*building* it. …*(she tests the words against ninety years and finds they fit exactly)* …I told *myself* I was *sorting.* that the *Wall* was *elsewhere*, a *great* *terrible* *elsewhere*, and I only *pointed.* …*(her hand leaves the pen)* …but the *pointing* *is* the *Wall.* isn't it. there's no *great* *machine* somewhere *else.* there's only *forty* of *me*, a *cycle*, at *posts* like *this*, all the way *down* the *causeway*, each of us *pointing* at the *easy* *dead* and *swearing* we don't make the *roll.* …*(she looks at you, and ninety years of flinch finally comes to rest)* …*then let it be reviewed*, Returned. *all* of it. I don't have the *standing* to *strike* a *quota* — but *you* were *given* *back*, and I have a *pen*, and I find, tonight, that I would *rather* be *emptied* from *my* *post* …than *fill* one *more* *quiet* *name.* …*(she picks the pen back up — to strike, now, not to fill)* …*tell* me which are *wrong.* …I have been *aching* …to *cross* *something* *out.*

nodes.speaker: the Sifter
nodes.text: *(The question — whose number is forty — makes her go very still, because it is the question under all the other questions, and she has spent ninety years not asking it.)* …*whose.* …*(slowly)* …the number comes *down* the *causeway.* from the *post* *above* *mine*, which got it from the *post* *above* *that.* I have *never* *seen* the *top* of the *stair.* …no *collector* has. that's *how* it *works* — no one *holds* the *whole* *number*, everyone holds a *piece*, and a *piece* of a *horror* feels like a *chore.* …*(her voice drops)* …but you *asked* who's *hungry.* …*(she glances up the causeway, into the grey)* …*something* *eats* the *walled*, Returned. the *unmade* don't just *stop* — they *feed* *something.* the quota isn't *bookkeeping.* it's a *harvest.* forty a *cycle*, from *every* *post*, *up* the *stair* to a *mouth* none of us have *seen* …*(and the old fear, but pointed now, useful)* …I *fill* a *plate*, Returned. I have *always* *known* it was a *plate.* …I only *pretended* …I *couldn't* *see* the *table.*

nodes.speaker: the Sifter
nodes.text: *(She nods, and her pen returns to the roll — but slower now, hovering, as if your mere attention has made the next name harder to write.)* …*aye.* …the *man* in the *coat.* …*(a flicker of something — not quite a smile)* …*watch* that one, Returned. he has *robbed* this *post* *four* *times* that I *know* of, and *twice* I only *noticed* *cycles* *later*, and *once* …*(she almost, almost smiles)* …*once* I think he *robbed* me of a *name* I was *glad* to *lose*, and *left* me *believing* I'd *struck* it *myself.* …*(the pen hovers)* …I do not *know* what he *is.* I know he has *no* *name* on *any* *roll* — I have *looked* — and that should make him *mine*, should make him *Wall*-*bound*, and *instead* …*(she shakes her head)* …*instead* he walks my *causeway* *free* and *steals* the *easy* *dead* off my *plate* …and I have *never* *once* …*managed* to *mind.*

nodes.speaker: a soul on the roll

variants.text: *(The midwife is looking at the roll — at the grey line struck through her own name — and she keeps touching the place on her chest where, a moment ago, a wall was waiting for her, as if to check it's really gone.)* …*struck.* …*(she says it like a woman saying a fever's broken)* …the man in the *coat* said — he said it was a *clerical* *matter.* that I'd been *filed* *wrong.* …*(she looks at you, and the competent hands are shaking now that they're allowed to)* …forty *years* I *caught* the *newborn*, Returned. the *faithful's* and the *faithless's*, in the *same* *bloody* *sheets*, and a *baby* doesn't *come* out *claimed*, it comes out *screaming* and *new* and *nobody's* — …*(fierce, tearful)* …and they were going to *wall* me for *keeping* my *hands* too *busy* to *pray.* …*(quietly)* …*thank* you. …*whatever* you *did.* …*whoever* that *man* *is.* …*tell* him — …*(she can't finish; she just presses her own hands together, the way she must have a thousand times, and nods)*

*(The midwife holds herself very still at the edge of the toll-post, watching the Sifter's pen the way a woman watches a rising tide she cannot outrun.)* …they *say* I'm for the *wall.* …*(bewildered, not yet even frightened, still stuck on the wrongness of it)* …I keep *asking* *what* I *did*, and the *clerk* says it isn't a *what*, it's a *category.* …a *category.* …*(she looks at her own hands)* …I *caught* this *town's* *children.* forty *years* of them. the *baker's*, the *priest's*, the *whore's*, the *lord's* — I never *once* asked whose *god* watched, because a *breech* *birth* at *midnight* doesn't *leave* you *time* to *check.* …*(and now the fear arrives, plain and terrible)* …is that the *category?* …*'too* *busy* *saving* *lives* to *kneel'?* …is *that* …the thing they *wall* you *for?*

choices.text: *(read the midwife on the roll — what forty years of catching the newborn made of a soul)* "Let me look at you a moment. All the way. Whatever the roll says, I want to see what's actually here."

*(the one who crosses — a promise from the soul the Wall gave back)* "Listen to me. I'm the one soul the Wall ever returned. I've seen both its sides. You do not belong on that roll, and I am going to see it struck — by review, by trick, by whatever it takes. You caught the priest's daughters. The cosmos can catch you for once."
"Tell me one of them, Orla. One birth. The one you'd want remembered if it came to that."
"Hold on. Don't move, don't sign anything. Let me deal with the man in the coat and the clerk."

nodes.speaker: a soul on the roll
nodes.text: *(You look, and your sense goes into forty years of midnights and finds a soul so plainly, unarguably worth keeping that the roll with her name on it becomes, in an instant, an obscenity.)* *(No grand faith. No god. Your sense reads instead the shape a life takes when it is spent entirely on the threshold where souls arrive: forty years of being the first hands a person ever felt, the one waiting on the near side of every birth in a whole town, godless not out of defiance but out of sheer occupied practicality — you cannot pray with your arms inside a labouring mother, and she never once resented the trade. And your sense reads the private theology she built without noticing, which is truer than most temples: that a newborn comes into the world claimed by no one, screaming and new and nobody's, and that this — the raw unclaimed aliveness of a thing just arrived — is not a lack to be corrected by some god's later stamp, but the holiest state there is, the brief clean moment before the world starts filing you. She spent forty years as the priestess of exactly that moment. And the Wall wants to file her under 'Faithless' — when the truth your sense reads is that she is the one soul in this toll-post who ever worshipped the unclaimed, on purpose, with her hands, at midnight, for free. If there is a category for that, it is not the one the Sifter wrote. It is the one the whole grey should have been built to protect.)*

nodes.speaker: a soul on the roll
nodes.text: *(You make the promise — you do not belong on that roll, and I will see it struck — and the midwife looks at you the way the mothers must have looked at her across forty years of hard midnights: with the specific, total trust of a soul who has just heard a competent voice say I have you.)* …*(she breathes, maybe for the first time since the clerk read her name)* …*by* *review.* *by* *trick.* …*(a wet, disbelieving laugh)* …you *sound* like the *man* in the *coat.* he said near the *same* — said the *cosmos* had *bad* *bookkeeping* and he'd been *correcting* it for *sport* since before my *town* had a *name.* …*(and then, steadier, the midwife's own hard-won creed)* …I *caught* the *breech* ones, Returned. the ones *turned* *wrong*, the ones the *other* *hands* gave *up* on. you *reach* *in*, and you *turn* the *child*, and you do *not* *let* *go* until it's *out* and *screaming.* …*(she meets your eyes)* …*so.* …I'm *turned* *wrong*, and the *other* *hands* gave *up.* …*(the ghost of forty years of stubborn competence)* …*don't* *let* *go.*

nodes.speaker: a soul on the roll
nodes.text: *(You ask for one birth, the one she'd want remembered, and the fear loosens its grip for a moment as the midwife does the thing she knows how to do better than anyone: she remembers a life arriving.)* …*(quiet, and then warmer)* …the *priest's* *second* *daughter.* the *hard* *winter.* …came *feet* *first* in the *dark*, cord *round* her *neck*, *blue* as a *drowned* *thing*, and the *priest* on his *knees* in the *next* *room* *praying* *loud* enough to *wake* the *dead* — …*(a small fierce smile)* …and I *thought*, *pray* all you *like*, *father*, but it's *my* *hands* in *here.* and I *turned* her, and I *cleared* her *throat* with my *own* *littlest* *finger*, and I *breathed* into her until she *screamed* — …*(she looks at her hands, wondering)* …and the *priest* came *in* and *wept* and *thanked* his *god.* …and I let him. …*(the smile steadies into something like grace)* …I never *needed* the *credit*, Returned. I just needed the *child* to *scream.* …*that's* the one. *Aefa*, they *named* her. she'd be *grey* *herself* by *now.* …*put* *that* on my *roll*, if there's to *be* one. …*not* *'faithless.'* …*'caught* *Aefa.* *breathing* by *dawn.'*

nodes.speaker: a soul on the roll
nodes.text: *(She nods, and goes still, and holds — the way she must have taught a thousand frightened mothers to hold, when the moment wasn't right yet and the only medicine was to wait.)* …*(a shaky breath)* …*hold.* …*aye.* I can *hold.* …*(a flicker of the competent woman under the fear)* …*told* enough *mothers* the *same*, in my *time.* *not* *yet*, love, *don't* *push* *yet*, *wait* for the *turn* — …*(she presses her hands together)* …*funny*, to be on *this* *end* of it. …*(and then, as you move toward the clerk and the man in the coat, she says the thing a midwife says, the only blessing she ever learned)* …*go* *on*, then. …I'll *breathe.* …*you* *do* the *turning.*
